title: The Erdős–Sós conjecture (Erdős Problem 548)
abstract: Proves the Erdős–Sós conjecture (1962), Erdős Problem 548: every graph on n ≥ k+1 vertices with at least (k−1)n/2 + 1 edges contains every tree on k+1 vertices as a (not necessarily induced) subgraph. The headline statement is the FrontierMath Erdős benchmark statement, reviewed by Thomas Bloom and carried verbatim by Google DeepMind's Formal Conjectures; the proof was found autonomously by GPT-6 Astra. It is a finite double counting over permutation words of the host vertices: rotating the first qualifying prefix of a cut word gives a gluing inequality for two rooted branches, and reversing the two blocks of a cut moves the root to a newly attached leaf. A strong induction on the order t of the tree bounds the adjacency-marked cut words by the rooted-copy count plus (t−2)·n!, so a tree-free host on n vertices has at most (t−2)n/2 edges, the sharp classical bound.

informal.Erdos548.erdos_548: Let n ≥ k+1. Every simple graph on n vertices with at least (k−1)n/2 + 1 edges contains every tree on k+1 vertices as a subgraph (an injective graph homomorphism). This is Erdős Problem 548, the Erdős–Sós conjecture, in the benchmark phrasing.
informal.Erdos548.tree_free_edge_bound: If a tree T on t ≥ 2 vertices is not contained in a graph G on n ≥ 1 vertices, then 2·|E(G)| ≤ (t−2)·n. This is the classical sharp form of the Erdős–Sós bound.
informal.Erdos548.rooted_word_tree_bound: For a tree T on t ≥ 2 vertices rooted at r, a host graph G and a nonempty repetition-free host word of length n, the number of cut permutation words of that word whose cut ends at a neighbour of the first letter is at most the number supporting a rooted copy of T on the prefix plus (t−2)·n!.
informal.Erdos548.marked_word_gluing_count: For a permutation-closed family W of repetition-free words, all of the same length m, and families A, B, C of letter sets with C ⊆ A and A R ∧ B X → C (R ∪ X) for disjoint R, X, the marked cuts (l, k) with l ∈ W and k ≤ m qualifying for A plus those qualifying for B number at most the allowed cuts plus those qualifying for C.
